Title: Record listing API returns HTTP 500 for every request
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Sign in as test@gmail.com / 12345
2. Open DevTools > Network, or call the API directly
3. POST https://dev.api.agnoshealth.com/api/ai_dashboard/dashboard with a valid JWT and the payload the UI sends
Expected Result: HTTP 200 with the record list, or 200 with an empty list if the account genuinely has no records.
Actual Result: HTTP 500 {"error_message":"internal_server_error"} every time. Reproduced across all three status values, every channel combination, with and without dates, with an empty body {} (which should be a 400), on a freshly issued token, and on three retries 20 minutes apart. The dashboard therefore shows 'Total cases : 0' permanently.
Related Test Cases: TC-GEN-02, TC-SRCH-01, TC-SRCH-03 to TC-SRCH-05, TC-FLT-01 to TC-FLT-13, TC-NAV-11, TC-NAV-12, TC-DL-05, TC-DL-06

Title: Logout does not clear the session token or patient PII from localStorage
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Sign in as test@gmail.com / 12345
2. Click Log Out and confirm the return to /ai_dashboard/login
3. Open DevTools > Application > Local Storage and inspect session, user, hospital and persist:root
Expected Result: Every authentication and patient-data key is removed, so the next person at the machine cannot recover the previous user's token or personal data.
Actual Result: Only user_name is removed. 'session' still holds a valid JWT access token; 'user' and 'persist:root' still hold e-mail, gender, date of birth, height, weight, age and name; 'hospital' still reads 12345. The token stays usable until it expires.

Title: Backend errors are rendered as an empty-data state
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Sign in and open the Diagnosis List while the listing API is returning 500
Expected Result: An error message such as 'Unable to load records, please try again', ideally with a retry action.
Actual Result: The page shows 'Total cases : 0' and the empty state 'ยังไม่มีข้อมูลการวินิจฉัย' - visually identical to a genuinely empty result. Nothing indicates the request failed.

Title: Failed login returns HTTP 500 instead of 401
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized (or 400) identifying the failure as bad credentials.
Actual Result: HTTP 500 {"error_message":"internal_server_error"}. Reproduced with a wrong password, an unknown user, and a malformed e-mail address. The UI maps any error to 'Wrong email or password', so a genuine outage would look identical to a typo.

Title: Password policy rejects '!' although the message says a special character is required
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open the sign-up page
2. Enter a unique e-mail and 'Passw0rd!' in both password fields
3. Click Confirm
4. Repeat with 'Passw0rd@'
Expected Result: 'Passw0rd!' is accepted - it is 9 characters with an uppercase letter, a digit and a special character, which is every rule the on-screen message states.
Actual Result: 'Passw0rd!' and 'Password1!' are rejected with the policy message; 'Passw0rd@' is accepted and creates the account (HTTP 200). Only the special character differs, so '!' is not in the implemented allow-list while '@' is.

Title: Password and Confirm Password share the DOM id 'password'
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open the sign-up page
2. Inspect both password inputs in DevTools
Expected Result: Unique id attributes, each associated with its visible label via <label for>.
Actual Result: Both inputs carry id='password'. Neither the sign-up nor the login inputs have a <label for> or aria-label, so they expose no accessible name. Duplicate ids are invalid HTML and break getElementById, label-click focus and screen readers.

Title: Confirming a download with no records does nothing
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Sign in and open the Diagnosis List while it shows 'Total cases : 0'
2. Click Download
3. Click ยืนยัน in the confirmation modal
Expected Result: Either the Download button is disabled when there is nothing to export, or the app reports that there is no data to export.
Actual Result: No network request is sent, no file is downloaded and no message is shown. The success toast 'Download CSV file successfully' sits in the DOM at opacity 0 and never fires. The modal stays open. Verified by listening for both the download event and any /api/ request for 20 s.
Evidence: docs/screenshots/recon-14-download.png; automated by TC-DL-03 and TC-DL-04

Title: Typographical errors in Thai and English UI copy
Steps to Reproduce:

2. Register a new account and read the confirmation message

Actual Result: The modal title reads 'ยินยันการดาวน์โหลด' and the post-registration message reads 'Please wait or account approval'.

Title: Dashboard routes respond with HTTP 404 while rendering the app
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open DevTools > Network
2. Navigate to /ai_dashboard, /ai_dashboard/login or /ai_dashboard/agnos/sign_up
Actual Result: The document responds 404 while the SPA still renders correctly, and the console logs 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404'. A static-hosting fallback serves index.html but keeps the 404 status. No user-visible impact, but wrong for crawlers, uptime monitors and status assertions.

Title: Selected status tab is not reflected in the URL
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Switch to the Completed tab
2. Press F5
Expected Result: The Completed tab is still selected after the reload.
Actual Result: The view resets to the default tab. Tab state lives only in component state, so it cannot be deep-linked, bookmarked, shared or restored after a refresh.

Title: Three triage values exist in the API but are never exposed in the UI
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Inspect the payload of POST /api/ai_dashboard/dashboard
2. Compare the triage array with the chips shown in the UI
Expected Result: The UI exposes every triage the backend can return, or the extra values are documented as intentionally hidden.
Actual Result: The request sends VISIT_PSYCO, VISIT_DEP_MENTAL_HEALTH and VISIT_DOCTOR alongside the five values the UI shows. Staff cannot filter on those three, so records carrying them may be hard to isolate.
